messages:
devon: FYI - noticed a regression on nightly perf runs. When KV prefetch is enabled together with our CUDA graph capture path on multi-GPU (8xA100) we see long all-reduce stalls and what looks like host-syncs breaking comm/compute overlap.

maria: ugh, any traces?

devon: pasted the minimal repro profile (nsys) below and a couple of nvprof nvtx ranges. it's most visible on medium-length sequences (seq=1024) and microbatch=1.

ranjit: can you drop the nsys command you ran? i'll try locally.

devon: sure - ran:```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run -t cuda,nvtx,cuda_memory --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-include=our_runtime:KV_PREFETCH_BEGIN,KV_PREFETCH_END ./bench --gpus 8 --seq 1024 --mb 1
```

maria: looking at the timeline screenshots - the capture/replay segment shows the graph capture stream doing host-side synchronization before the NCCL all-reduce starts. that lines up with a stream semantics mismatch: our KV prefetch uses an external stream we register into graph capture, but the all-reduce is on the internal compute stream and appears to wait.

ranjit: i'm seeing repeated `cudaStreamSynchronize` at capture boundaries in the trace. maybe our capture wrapper is calling synchronize to flush host copies when prefetch queue is non-empty.

ashley: iirc we added a safety sync to avoid races when prefetch inflight buffers are reused. might be the change that regressed overlap.

ci-bot: CI nightly #2145: perf-regression detected (+18% tail latency) for model resnet-like-kv-workload.

maria: quick hypothesis: during cudaGraph capture we are merging an external prefetch stream into the graph with streamCaptureModeGlobal, but our memory reuse pool relies on host barriers. when capture replays, the replay enqueues ops in the capture stream but the host-side barrier forces a sync before the NCCL all-reduce gets issued on the compute stream -> kills overlap.

ranjit: possible fixes: 1) avoid registering the external prefetch stream into graph capture and instead emit prefetch ops on the compute stream during capture; 2) remove the host sync by switching to device-side fences (cudaEvent with inter-stream dependencies) during prefetch; 3) disable graph capture for workloads with microbatch=1.

devon: i prototyped #1 locally: changed kv_prefetch to use compute stream when within a capture scope by checking `cudaGraphIsCapturing()` and falling back. result: overlap restored in the simple repro, tail latency back to baseline. no host syncs in timeline.

ashley: interesting. any downside? do we risk larger & more frequent interference between prefetch and compute kernels?

devon: tradeoff: prefetch on compute stream can contend with decode kernels but keeps things within one capture graph - no sync needed. will need to tune batching heuristics to avoid hurting latency for larger microbatches.

maria: can you paste the small diff you used?

devon:```cpp
// runtime/prefetch.cpp (sketch)
if (cudaGraphIsCapturing()) {
  // route into the compute stream to avoid external-stream capture semantics
  launch_prefetch_on(stream_compute, buf, len);
} else {
  launch_prefetch_on(stream_prefetch, buf, len);
}
```

ranjit: thanks. i want to try option #2 (device-side events) as well. device events would avoid host sync but still allow the prefetch to be on a separate stream.

ashley: could we add a guard in kernel-selection: if microbatch==1 && kv_prefetch_enabled && cuda_graph_enabled, select non-cudagraph path (i.e., fallback to replayless-mode)? that might be the least risky short-term mitigation.

maria: agrees for immediate mitigation. long-term we should make capture semantics robust. add a flag `runtime.capture_prefetch_policy` with options `auto|inline|external` so teams can test.

devon: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3145 (WIP) - implements compute-stream fallback inside prefetch and a runtime flag. includes nsys samples.

ci-bot: PR 3145 created by devon - label: perf/regression.

ranjit: i'll try device-event prototype later today and post traces. if device events work we can keep prefetch parallelism without host sync.

maria: also add an nvtx range around NCCL allreduce and export `NCCL_PROTO` so we can see whether collective enters a slower protocol after capture (some hardware picks different PTX paths in capture).

devon: good call. timeline showed all-reduce switching to LL128 fallback in a couple of captures. adding nvtxs now.

ashley: assigning owners: devon -> short-term mitigation PR, ranjit -> device-event prototype and perf trace, maria -> add NVTX and run expanded nightly tests. i'll shepherd canary release if fixes look good.

devon: thanks. will push an updated PR with tests that run our microbatch=1 seq=1024 scenario in the harness.

ranjit: fyi, i saw similar weirdness on 4xT4 repro at lower seq when capture + prefetch enabled yesterday. might be common across archs.

maria: OK — let's treat this as a perf-incident with follow-up: 1) short-term runtime guard; 2) device-event approach for correctness+parallelism; 3) more conservative kernel-picker heuristics for capture-mode.

devon: will bump priority. posting the nsight screenshots in thread. :eyes:

ashley: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
